content.text: Intent
Describe what this spec is for.
Scope
What is IN, and what is explicitly OUT (non-goals).
Scenarios
The journeys this must support, S1..Sn — each a sequence of steps with its branches and error paths. A scenario may be a person's journey or an automated process; it needs no screen.
Requirements
Numbered R1..Rn — WHAT, one requirement each, never HOW. An always-true invariant is numbered P1..Pn.
Data model
The business nouns this needs: key attributes IN BUSINESS TERMS, relationships, and uniqueness or lifecycle rules. No Java types, no columns, no widgets.
User interface
The screens this needs and how they should feel: purpose, key interactions, and any layout or look you have an opinion about — prose, a sketch, or an HTML mock.
Dependencies
What this relies on: other specs, existing entities, external systems or services.
Constraints
Rules the implementation must obey: security, performance targets, expected volume, cost, latency, locale, compliance. "None." is a valid, explicit answer.
Acceptance criteria
Numbered A1..An — each TESTABLE (pass/fail decidable), each naming the requirement(s) it verifies. Prefer "WHEN [trigger], the system SHALL [response]".
Migration & compatibility
What happens to what already exists — rows, users, callers: backfilled, defaulted, or grandfathered?
Artifacts
What will exist when done: entities, screens, services, migrations, docs.
Open Questions
The clarification ledger: every assumption becomes a question here, and is REPLACED by the decision once one is made — never silently filled in.
